correctness.rationale: The image of the adjacency is exactly the span W of the two defect coordinates and two nondefect shore sums. When (a-1)(b-1) is nonzero modulo 3, the first four iterates of a defect coordinate span W, and W splits off the kernel. When one shore coefficient vanishes, the nondefect coordinate test forces a zero-primary exponent of three; when both vanish A^3=0 but A^2 is nonzero. For a cyclic adjacency block with coordinate x, (u,v) maps to tu-v in the quadratic module with t^2-xt+1=0, and the update is multiplication by t. Thus t^deg(f) f(t+t^-1) is the exact temporal invariant factor, and a cyclic generator on a maximal block realizes the order, over every stated extension field. Cyclotomic orders and the least power of 3 killing each primary multiplicity give all six residue orders and the size-four exception. The two disjoint squarefree sectors of orders 5 and 10 plus the order-4 kernel sector give the fixed dimensions, Möbius census and maximal-period probability. Independent exact matrix tests covered all six residues and the exception, and 200 fixed-dimension comparisons at five doubly-two pairs and times 1–40. value.rationale: A single missing edge gives an exact perturbation problem for a natural reversible dynamics. The classification distinguishes prime-to-3 sectors from characteristic-dependent Jordan resonances, explains why the order can rise to 36 or fall to 10, and yields quantitative period statistics in an infinite residue class. This is more than restating the known real adjacency spectrum.
